rv.q: Calhoun’s “Black Cypress Bayou” is packed with cultural richness, and trauma, but never feels too heavy.
Black Cypress Bayou is not simply entertaining, it is invigorating.

Ratcliff's unfussy direction on the small but atmospheric set...delineates the balance between past and present, comic and tragic, real and imagined that makes Black Cypress Bayou a place of mystery and revelation.
For Definition Theatre, Black Cypress Bayou highlights the stellar abilities of Black women—their voices, presence, and vision—as framed by a theatrical magic borrowed from the bayou.

The all-female cast, led by the outstanding talents of Michelle Renee Bester (LadyBird), Rita Wicks (RaeMeka), RJW Mays (Vernita), and Jyreika Guest as Taysha, delivered a truly engaging and captivating performance that made this 90-minute production a true find.
Toss in some history, supernatural happenings, and family drama and I'm on board.

cn.t: Critics praise Calhoun's assured dark comedy as a striking discovery, blending supernatural southern gothic with sharp family drama. The swampy setting proves a potent metaphor, with strong performances elevating this emotionally precise exploration of trauma and secrets.
